user_scenario: A Split PDF workflow receives a PDF containing many pages or dense identifier text; page excerpts are sent to the split planner.
expected_behavior: The aggregate page-text payload respects MAX_FILE_PARSE_INPUT_TOKENS, or an oversized input is explicitly rejected before the model call.
observed_behavior: The unmodified helper produces 693300 tokens for 300 dense pages and 275000 tokens for 1100 short pages against a 256000-token limit. A two-page control preserves its text and page numbers.
root_cause: Per-page truncation slices characters after checking tokens; the 256-token minimum allocation also exceeds the global budget for enough pages. Neither branch bounds the aggregate.
entry_path: SplitPdfBlock.execute lines 458-479 validates and reads the PDF without a page-count cap
_build_page_texts lines 178-190 computes the returned page payload
_request_split_plan lines 206-220 injects all page_texts into the split-pdf prompt and hands it to the configured LLM handler
preserved_behaviors: Every input page remains identifiable; choosing rejection versus smaller per-page excerpts requires a maintainer decision
design_uncertainties: How to preserve meaningful excerpts for extremely many pages while respecting the aggregate cap; no implementation chosen
